content.title: Iran Deal Q&A
content.text: Want to know what’s in the Iran deal and how it works? Here are the answers to a few questions you might have on how we will make sure that Iran’s nuclear program remains exclusively peaceful. "Anytime, anywhere" inspections sound good. Why doesn’t this deal require those? Is this a "bad deal"? Shouldn't we have just walked away from the table and kept the interim deal in place? Did we just take whatever deal we could get, because we wanted this deal too much? Why is Iran allowed any uranium enrichment? Does this deal sunset? And if it does, doesn't that mean Iran can have nuclear weapon when it does? Does this deal do anything about the U.S. citizens detained in Iran or address any of our other problems with Iran, like terrorism? Is there a "secret" or "side" deal that the U.S. agreed to with Iran? Is Congress and the public seeing what it should see? Does the world stand with the U.S. in supporting this deal? Won’t this deal create a regional arms race? If we’re lifting the arms embargo in 5 years and missile restrictions in 8 years, doesn’t that mean the U.S. has given up on countering Iran’s destabilizing activities? Won’t Iran get $150 billion from sanctions relief, and won’t that money go straight toward terrorist activity in the region? Shouldn’t we just go back to more sanctions? The rest of the world will go along with us. Is the U.S. delisting Qassam Soleimani and the IRGC under the JCPOA? Did Iran receive a $100 billion signing bonus with this deal? Has the United States betrayed Israel on the Iran deal? Why didn’t the deal stick to the framework announced in Lausanne? Will companies that sign contracts with Iran be able to continue that business even if Iran violates the JCPOA and snapback occurs, because of a "grandfather clause"? Does the deal require the P5+1 to defend Iran’s nuclear program from attack? How is this deal any different than the deal with North Korea? Will Iran be able to inspect its own nuclear facilities?
